equivalent: EQUIVALENT, not a hole. `dot` is the sum over ascending `i` of `w[i*n+a] * w[i*n+b]`; swapping a and b commutes each product and leaves the summation order alone, so dot(a,b) and dot(b,a) are bit-identical for ANY contents of the public `w` field -- the symmetry is in the construction of `dot`, not in any matrix a constructor happens to accept, so no asymmetric precision is reachable. The double loop visits every ordered pair, so the mutant writes dot(a,b) into position (b,a) exactly where the original writes dot(b,a) into that same position, and the two values are the same bits. The one position written twice is the diagonal (a,a), reached in both versions at the single iteration b = a of outer step a, before that step's `+= 1.0 / var_prior`, and never written again at any later a (b*n+a == c*n+c forces b = c = a). The reads are untouched, so a `w` shortened through the public field panics at the same index in both. MEASURED with a standalone fixture running both bodies: 1,258 cases over n_obs, n_lat in 1..6 with random weights, plus a lopsided w of subnormals, zeros, +/-1e300 and 1e-320 -- every entry bit-identical.

equivalent: EQUIVALENT, not a hole. The loop runs l DOWN to 0 and the guarded assignment is the last statement of the body, so at l = 0 the value stored in `delta` is read by nothing: the loop then ends and the function returns `grads`, which was written earlier in that same body. The extra pass also cannot fail where the original returns -- its only fallible reads are `self.w[0][i * n_in + j]` for i < sizes[1] and j < sizes[0], which is exactly the index range `predict_layer(0, ..)` already read in the `forward` call at the head of `backprop`, so any `w[0]` short enough to make it panic has already panicked before the backward pass starts; `x[0][j]` for j < sizes[0] was likewise already read. MEASURED with a standalone fixture running both bodies: 200 cases over the layer shapes [2,3,1], [4,6,5,3], [1,1], [3,1,1,2,4] and [5,2] with random weights, inputs and targets -- every gradient bit-identical.
